item backdrop=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/100595-2f3234ce-61ff-508f-acbc-48b6bf17bc3c_preview.jpg | channel=The Matrix Conference 2026 | date=2026-10-22T10:45:00Z | duration=1380 | id=ccc:2f3234ce-61ff-508f-acbc-48b6bf17bc3c | image=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/100595-2f3234ce-61ff-508f-acbc-48b6bf17bc3c_preview.jpg | kind=0 | plot=Side effects of modern healthcare communication: data breaches, €1.2 billion in GDPR fines last year, and a group chat with 47 nurses. The treatment is a messaging app. The one you're thinking of isn't it.

Walk into any ward, GP surgery, home care team, or therapy practice in Europe and you'll find the same thing: clinicians on WhatsApp. Not because they don't know better — because it works, it's fast, and the secure alternative breaks the workflow. This talk is a frank look at why Europe's most-used clinical tool isn't a clinical tool.

The answer cuts across the entire care continuum: from large hospital trusts wrestling with security friction to mobile nurses no IT policy ever quite reaches. GDPR enforcement is tightening. AI may be the first thing that genuinely tips the balance between convenience and compliance. This talk takes a European perspective and asks what it will genuinely take to move healthcare off WhatsApp: better products, smarter regulation, open standards, or all three.

The side door works. The fortress doesn't.

This is a talk about three people.

Amira is a home care nurse. Her "ward" is eleven living rooms and a car. Nobody from IT has ever been in any of them. Mateo is a hospital nurse on night shift — issued a phone, a pager, and a login that expires every 8 hours. Dr. Chen is a doctor. Always reachable, never has time.

Three people, three employers, three different IT policies. Same behaviour: they all use WhatsApp. Not because they don't know better. Because the secure alternative is slower, harder, and breaks the workflow that actually keeps patients safe.

This talk walks through the data. What the research says about clinician use of consumer messaging apps. What regulators have actually done about it (€1.2B in GDPR fines last year, healthcare enforcement up 26%). And why dedicated solutions built on open standards like Matrix — including the CGM Messenger and CGM TI-Messenger shipping into European healthcare — are still sitting at | ref=ccc:2f3234ce-61ff-508f-acbc-48b6bf17bc3c | source=ccc | subtitle=Patrice Zoe Brend'amour | title=Side Effects Include: Data Breaches, GDPR Fines, and a Group Chat With 47 Nurses
item backdrop=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/102423-2d34bdcf-3fef-503a-add2-62b085fb454a_preview.jpg | channel=The Matrix Conference 2026 | date=2026-10-22T09:45:00Z | duration=1146 | id=ccc:2d34bdcf-3fef-503a-add2-62b085fb454a | image=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/102423-2d34bdcf-3fef-503a-add2-62b085fb454a_preview.jpg | kind=0 | plot=Matrix was designed around strong end-to-end encryption and user-controlled trust. While this model is ideal for private communication, large public-sector and critical infrastructure deployments face additional requirements that go beyond traditional E2EE.

This talk explores the challenges of operating Matrix within one of Europe's largest sovereign and security-critical IT infrastructures, where legal archiving obligations, compliance requirements, incident handling, automation and long-term information governance must coexist with modern encrypted communication.

We discuss why classic end-to-end encryption is not always sufficient in enterprise environments and examine the concept of End-to-Organization Encryption (E2OE) as a potential architectural approach. Rather than focusing solely on technical implementation, the session evaluates the trade-offs between confidentiality, organizational trust, operational resilience and regulatory compliance.

Topics include message archiving, eDiscovery, compliance scanning, bot integration, fall handling, key recovery, device loss, and organizational access models. We will also discuss how these requirements influence Matrix client architecture, headless clients, encryption key management and federation.

The presentation is intended for Matrix developers, infrastructure architects, security professionals and public-sector operators interested in deploying Matrix at national scale while balancing sovereignty, usability and compliance.

item backdrop=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/92092-0d98e3c5-9b4d-5200-ba6a-53442b043d13_preview.jpg | channel=The Matrix Conference 2026 | date=2026-10-22T12:15:00Z | duration=1461 | id=ccc:0d98e3c5-9b4d-5200-ba6a-53442b043d13 | image=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/92092-0d98e3c5-9b4d-5200-ba6a-53442b043d13_preview.jpg | kind=0 | plot=Are you operating a large server, bridge or bot? Are you managing lots of spaces or rooms?
Do you sometimes need to modify rooms outside of your regular account?
Try Matrix Wrench. It's is a powerful, open-source web app to view and edit room states. It works with access tokens from users and AppServices.

In my time at the Matrix.org bridges team, I had worked on a few of the largest bridges operated at the time. Routine tasks included supporting the community leaders, e.g. when room admins had made mistakes or became inactive.
With the administrator role of the bridge bot, we we're able to modify the room state, revoke rights and promote new community leaders to administrators.

What started as a lot of manual, error-prone work in the terminal with curl became a web app written for the job. It allowed us as operators and community managers to tweak the rooms easier and faster.
Wrong permissions? View them. Fix them.
Wrong room visibility? Easy fix.
Lots of unwanted accounts? Kick them at once.
Migrate a community to a new room? Copy the state and members you want.

Matrix Wrench is closely built around the Matrix API endpoint. Most buttons only fire one network request. Many actions have simple forms, so you don't need to look up the Matrix Spec in a hurry. And if you want to replicate any of the actions in Matrix Wrench, e.g. for an automated script, you can have a look at its Network Manager which shows a curl command for all performed requests.

In this talk, we'll explore recent additions to the SDK, including threads,
spaces, QR code login, shared encrypted history, migration from Element Classic

behind them, and some of the lessons learned along the way.

This talk is aimed at Matrix developers and contributors who are interested in
the evolution of the Matrix Rust SDK. The focus will be on the design and
implementation behind several major features that have recently landed in the
SDK.

The Matrix Rust SDK is one of the most complete SDK in the world. It's becoming really mature: more and more clients are relying on it due to its great features, stability, and performance. Maybe you want to give it a try for your own great client? To illustrate our point, we demonstrate how to develop a Matrix CLI client from scratch with the Rust SDK, step by step, up to having a fully functional client, with a room list, a timeline, the ability to send and to receive messages, along with full end-to-end encryption support. We will use the following components: `SyncService`, `RoomListService`, `Timeline`, `SendQueue`, `EventCache` and so on.

item backdrop=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/98015-c1f47b54-bc32-51c6-b634-4ab1ac4fd18f_preview.jpg | channel=The Matrix Conference 2026 | date=2026-10-22T14:15:00Z | duration=1571 | id=ccc:c1f47b54-bc32-51c6-b634-4ab1ac4fd18f | image=https://static.media.ccc.de/media/events/matrix-conf/2026/98015-c1f47b54-bc32-51c6-b634-4ab1ac4fd18f_preview.jpg | kind=0 | plot=Matrix was created with the idea of federation at the core, but nowadays there is matrix.org which contains a majority of the users of the wider matrix network, nullifying the benefits of it. This has since also started generating significant cost for The Matrix Foundation and lead to shutdown of some previously offered bridges. The Homeserver Decentralisation Working Group aims to improve the situation.

One of the co-chairs of the Homeserver Decentralisation Working Group go on a little journey through the history of the WG, how it formed, what challenges it tries to master and what lies ahead.

After a little introduction, you'll hear
- about the events that lead to the creation of the Working Group,
- how the initial members met,
- what problems The Matrix Foundation was already facing,
- what goals we have,
- what challenges lie ahead of us,
- our produced documents, governance proposals, tooling and general milestones achieved
- offering a look into the future, on what we aim to do in the near future and what we hope the far future will look like.

This talk is intended for Matrix contributors, homeserver administrators, community organizers, client developers and anyone interested in the governance and long-term sustainability of the Matrix ecosystem but also bigger organizations, that want to learn about the real benefits of federation and consider opening up their instance.

_In case you don't know about the Working Group, you can find all our information [here](https://github.com/cleverer/matrix-wg-promote-alternative-homeservers) or ask in our [matrix room](https://matrix.to/#/%23homeserver-decentralisation:matrix.org)._

This talk presents MSG GOV, a Matrix-based messaging platform for the Brazilian federal government. Today, it targets a defined set of public servants rather than the entire population or every government employee — a deliberate, controlled scope as the platform matures. We plan to share the factors that drove the need for a sovereign messaging app in the first place and to dig into how MSG GOV is built and run. The solution is designed to operate on SERPRO's sovereign cloud, the Brazilian government's own cloud infrastructure, with all the operational and trust implications that entail. At the center of the talk is identity: how MSG GOV integrates with gov.br, Brazil's national single-sign-on system, through a dedicated user management module we developed to bridge gov.br authentication with Matrix accounts.
